papers.abstract_en: Mitigating on-target off-tumor toxicity remains a central challenge for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy for solid tumors. We developed a hypoxia-inducible CAR-T-cell product targeting carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) that restricts CAR activation to hypoxic tumor niches via oxygen-dependent expression control. In this first-in-human, phase I trial enrolling heavily pretreated patients with relapsed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), a single infusion of the investigational product achieved an objective response rate of 47% and a disease control rate of 87%, with a manageable safety profile. Exploratory analyses showed that clinical outcomes were associated with baseline factors. Deep single-cell profiling indicated that the clinical response was associated with the expansion of hypoxia-adapted, tumor-reactive-like CD8+ T cells alongside coordinated functional maturation of natural killer (NK) cells. Collectively, these data provide clinical proof-of-concept for hypoxia-inducible CAR design and inform the rational development of strategies leveraging tumor microenvironmental features in solid tumor cellular immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Interim analysis of the Neotorch study demonstrated significant benefit in event-free survival (EFS) and major pathological response (MPR) rate for perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable Stage Ⅲ non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, we report the final analysis results of the overall Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients from this study. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients with treatment-naïve resectable Stage II, or Stage IIIA, IIIB (N2) NSCLC, were randomized to receive toripalimab or placebo plus chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment (3 cycles), adjuvant treatment (1 cycle), and toripalimab or placebo monotherapy as maintenance treatment (up to 13 cycles). The primary endpoints of this study were EFS assessed by investigators and MPR evaluated by blinded independent pathologic review (BIPR) in Stage Ⅲ patients, as well as the overall Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients. RESULTS: A total of 501 patients in China were randomized (toripalimab arm: N=250, placebo arm: N=251). The baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the 2 arms. At the final analysis (median follow-up of 48.2 months), the investigator-assessed EFS was significantly improved in the toripalimab arm with stratified hazard ratio (HR) of 0.52 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.39, 0.68; stratified P <0.0001), and the median EFS in the toripalimab arm was not reached, while 20.2 months in the placebo arm. The inter-arm difference of MPR rate was statistically significant and clinically meaningful (47% vs 9%, P<0.0001). The OS prolongation was also statistically significant in the toripalimab arm (HR 0.66; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.89, P=0.0072), with median survival not reached in either arm. The safety profile was consistent with the interim analysis, with no new safety signals identified. CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy demonstrated durable and significant benefits on EFS, MPR, and OS in resectable Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ NSCLC patients, with a manageable safety profile.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In the DeLLphi-304 trial, at a median follow-up of <12 months, tarlatamab significantly improved overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and patient-reported outcomes (PROs), and demonstrated a favorable safety profile versus chemotherapy. We report efficacy and safety outcomes after extended follow-up in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this phase 3, open-label trial, patients with SCLC whose disease had progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy were randomized (1:1) to receive either tarlatamab or chemotherapy (topotecan, lurbinectedin, or amrubicin) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death. The primary endpoint was OS. Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed PFS, objective response, disease control, duration of response per RECIST v1.1, PROs, and safety. RESULTS: As of data cutoff (18 February 2026), median OS was 13.6 and 8.4 months with tarlatamab and chemotherapy, respectively (median follow-up, 23.3 and 22.8 months). Median PFS was 4.2 and 3.2 months, respectively (median follow-up, 22.2 and 21.9 months). Kaplan-Meier estimated OS rates at 12/24 months were 55.9%/30.3% with tarlatamab versus 39.0%/14.9% with chemotherapy; corresponding PFS rates at 12/24 months were 20.6%/14.2% versus 5.9%/2.3%. Objective response rate was 35.4% with tarlatamab, including six confirmed complete responses versus 20.4% with chemotherapy; at data cutoff, ongoing responses were observed in 31.1% (28/90) versus 3.8% (2/52) of responders, respectively. Sustained disease control for ≥52 weeks was observed in 24.4% versus 4.3%. Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 3.2% versus 6.6%; grade ≥3 events decreased over time, with no serious TRAEs with onset ≥12 months. CRS and ICANS occurred early in treatment and were predominantly low grade. CONCLUSIONS: With extended follow-up, tarlatamab continues to demonstrate sustained and durable clinical benefit and a favorable long-term tolerability profile versus chemotherapy, in patients with SCLC after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, supporting its use as the standard of care in this setting.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116. FINDINGS: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group. INTERPRETATION: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population. FUNDING: Baili-Bio (Chengdu) Pharmaceutical.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. METHODS: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting. FUNDING: Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis. METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment. INTERPRETATION: Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis. FUNDING: aTyr and Kyorin.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated. RESEARCH QUESTION: Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up. RESULTS: Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline. INTERPRETATION: Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

papers.abstract_en: Barrett's esophagus (BE) patients require improved cancer risk stratification to identify high-risk individuals while reducing over-treatment in low-risk populations. BE evolution towards adenocarcinoma is likely driven by a combination of genomic and microenvironmental factors, suggesting the potential of predictive models that integrate both. Here, we developed BEACON (Barrett's Esophagus DNA content Abnormality and immune ecology for Cancer Outcome), a spatially aware framework integrating deep learning-based prediction of DNA content and immune architecture from routine histopathology. First, DACOR, a multi-instance learning model that predicts DNA content from histopathology, was trained using 777 BE biopsies with flow cytometry-based DNA content data scanned at two institutions, and it demonstrated strong performance across both validation and test datasets for DNA content abnormality prediction. Patients classified as DNA content abnormal by DACOR demonstrated increased cancer progression. Complementary models for cell classification and tissue segmentation enabled spatial immune ecology metric computations. Abnormal regions exhibited increased lymphoplasmacytic inflammation versus normal regions. Among patients with DNA content abnormality, cancer progressors exhibited increased plasma cell clustering adjacent to abnormal epithelium compared to non-progressors. Finally, a logistic regression model was developed that integrated molecular, immune ecological, and epithelial morphology features for cancer risk stratification. The integrated risk classification model stratified DNA content abnormal patients into high- and low-risk groups that corresponded with progression and patient survival. Overall, BEACON spatially integrates molecular abnormality with immune ecology to stratify BE patients by cancer progression risk using routine pathology images.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis disease clusters within households, but the proportion of disease among household contacts that results from recent within-household transmission remains unclear. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact, and the proportion of all tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission. METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we included empirical studies or systematic reviews published in English from Jan 1, 1985, to Jan 26, 2024, that described at least ten pairs of individuals with a history of household contact, in which both people had active tuberculosis and their isolates were strain-typed using RFLP, mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat, or whole-genome sequencing. We excluded studies that only collected data on residence for isolates of the same strain and studies that used preselection for both index and secondary cases. Searches of MEDLINE, Embase, Global Health, Web of Science, and POPLINE databases were updated on Jan 26, 2024. Titles and abstracts and then full texts were screened, and data were extracted independently, by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Summary data were extracted from published reports; when necessary, we contacted study authors, some of whom reanalysed data. The main outcome was the prevalence of strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact. Our main analyses excluded studies using 12-loci or 15-loci mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat and studies performed during tuberculosis outbreaks, as these were considered to be at high risk of bias. We used an inverse variance heterogeneity model applying a double-arcsine transformation to stabilise variance. The proportion of total variability due to between-study heterogeneity was estimated using I2. We estimated the proportion of all tuberculosis attributable to recent household transmission as the product of strain concordance and the proportion of all cases in the community with a history of household exposure to a putative index case, which we derived from external data. Sensitivity analyses assessed robustness to the choice of model and to varying assumptions about household size when estimating the attributable fraction. Our PROSPERO registration number was CRD42024504096. FINDINGS: The updated searches identified an additional 3735 unique records. Thirty studies from 18 countries met the inclusion criteria. Four studies were omitted from the meta-analysis because they were at high risk of bias. The remaining 26 studies comprised 1544 index-secondary patient pairs. A high proportion of total variability was due to between-study heterogeneity (I2 90·3, 95% CI 69·0-95·3%). The overall pooled estimate of the prevalence of strain discordance was 0·47 (95% CI 0·32-0·62). Pooled estimates differed by tuberculosis incidence: 0·30 (0·25-0·34) in low-incidence settings, 0·25 (0·15-0·36) in moderate-incidence settings, and 0·59 (0·41-0·76) in high-incidence settings (p=0·003). The median proportion of tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission was 10·8% (range 1·4-21·1%). INTERPRETATION: Strain discordance is common, particularly in high-incidence settings. These findings suggest that recent household transmission makes a small contribution to the overall burden of tuberculosis disease. In this study, the number of household pairs and geographical diversity of the studies were strengths. Between-study heterogeneity limited precision. Our estimates of attributable fraction relied on external data. Strain discordance does not necessarily imply discordance in drug susceptibility. These results should motivate a greater focus on social protection and interrupting community transmission. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a severe vascular disorder, is closely associated with chronic inflammatory states and oxidative stress. Myeloid differentiation protein 2 (MD2), a key co-receptor of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), is well established in mediating various inflammation-driven pathologies. However, its role in pulmonary hypertension and its potential involvement in oxidative stress regulation remain unclear. METHODS AND RESULTS: MD2 expression was upregulated in both PH patients and murine PH models. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of MD2 improved hemodynamic parameters, attenuated pulmonary vascular remodeling, and reduced right ventricular hypertrophy. MD2 inhibition significantly reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that suppression of the membrane protein MD2 activated intracellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, leading to enhanced peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activity. PPARγ, in turn, suppressed nuclear transcription of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), resulting in a marked reduction in mitochondrial oxidative stress. CONCLUSION: This study indicates that MD2 may act as an upstream regulator of mitochondrial oxidative stress in PH. Inhibition of MD2 attenuates pulmonary hypertension through activation of the AMPK/PPARγ axis, which suppresses NOX4 mediated mitochondrial oxidative stress. Targeting MD2 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for PH.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Uncontrolled pneumonia induced by influenza virus infection results in severe lung pathology. Timely and proper tissue self-repair is critical to improve survival. This study aimed to identify probiotic strains that confer protection against acute lung injury induced by influenza virus infection and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Significant structural alterations in the gut microbiota were observed in influenza patients, characterized by a marked depletion in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, whose abundance was negatively correlated with disease severity. In a murine model of influenza infection, oral administration of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and its culture supernatant markedly alleviated lung injury. Targeted metabolomic analysis identified butyrate as the principal metabolite produced by Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that mediates lung tissue protection. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that butyrate promotes the differentiation of pulmonary CD4⁺T cells into a reparative phenotype with enhanced interleukin-22 (IL-22) production. Mechanistically, butyrate facilitates IL-22 secretion through monounsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis via a histone-acetylation-dependent NR4A1-SCD1 axis. Accumulated monounsaturated fatty acids further enhance mitochondrial activities, which are essential for robust IL-22 production. Utilizing an IL-22 knockout mouse model, we confirmed the indispensable protective role of IL-22 in this gut-lung axis during influenza infection. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that butyrate, derived from intestinal commensal Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, plays a crucial role in maintaining pulmonary tissue homeostasis during influenza infection by modulating intrinsic lipid metabolism in CD4+T cells. This study underscores the promising translational potential of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii supplementation as an innovative therapeutic strategy for severe influenza-associated lung injury. papers.abstract_en: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined. OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH. METHODS: Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models. CONCLUSIONS: The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

papers.abstract_en: APOBEC3 cytosine deaminases are major sources of cancer mutations. In lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), APOBEC3 activity drives tumor evolution and therapy resistance, nominating these enzymes as therapeutic targets. Although APOBEC3A drives most APOBEC3-associated mutational signature burden across cancers, the relative contributions of individual paralogs in LUAD remain unclear. Here, we define the roles of endogenously misregulated APOBEC3 deaminases using CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts and whole-genome sequencing of 197 long-term propagated single-cell clones. APOBEC3 mutagenesis falls into three patterns, driven predominantly by APOBEC3A, by both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, or minimal despite detectable enzyme expression. Commonly used surrogate measures, including mRNA and protein levels and in vitro deaminase activity, do not predict these contributions. We also provide the first causal evidence that endogenous APOBEC3A generates the indel signature InD9a, linking it to uracil excision following cytosine deamination. These heterogeneous contributions highlight the need for biomarkers that resolve individual APOBEC3 activities to guide therapeutic targeting.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Risk in interstitial pneumonia (IP) is assessed routinely by the Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) score from pulmonary function and the tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) on echocardiography. This study evaluated whether the percent perfusion defect (%PPD) on short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold (STDIBH) pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT carries prognostic information that neither captures. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety-one consecutive patients with IP who underwent STDIBH perfusion SPECT/CT between 2012 and 2023 were analyzed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was a composite major adverse event (MAE) of all-cause death, acute exacerbation of IP, respiratory-failure hospitalization, and initiation of home oxygen therapy. Association was assessed by Cox regression and discrimination by censoring-weighted time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: MAE occurred in 66 of 91 patients (72.5%) over a median follow-up of 45.9 months. %PPD was associated with MAE after adjustment for the GAP score and antifibrotic therapy (adjusted hazard ratio 1.2304 per 10 percentage points, 95% CI 1.0568-1.4325; P = 0.008), and, in exploratory analyses, for TRPG and the GAP score together (1.2058, 1.0314-1.4096; P = 0.019). It showed no significant correlation with TRPG (Spearman r = 0.164; P = 0.140). Time-dependent discrimination did not differ significantly between %PPD and the GAP score at 6, 12, and 24 months, and adding %PPD to the GAP score changed the Harrell C-index from 0.692 to 0.719 (difference 0.027, 95% CI - 0.009 to 0.107). %PPD was obtained in all 91 patients and the GAP score in 68 (74.7%). CONCLUSION: In IP, %PPD measures a dimension of risk that the GAP score does not capture, and exploratory analyses suggest that echocardiography does not capture it either. %PPD is obtainable when the GAP score is not. Its discrimination did not differ significantly from that of the GAP score, and adding it to the GAP score did not significantly improve discrimination.

papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive, and fatal fibrotic lung disease with a poor prognosis. While epigenetic regulation is increasingly recognized as a key driver of fibrogenesis, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unclear. In this study, we identify PR domain-containing protein 16 (PRDM16) as a critical epigenetic repressor of profibrotic gene transcription. PRDM16 expression is significantly downregulated in lungs of IPF patients, in TGF-β1-activated fibroblasts, and in bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse models. Functional analyses demonstrate that fibroblast-specific Prdm16 deletion promotes the progression of pulmonary fibrosis following BLM treatment. In contrast, overexpression of full-length PRDM16 or its truncated variant (PRDM16ΔPR-ZF1) attenuates the fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, thereby mitigating BLM-induced fibrotic phenotypes. Mechanistically, PRDM16 binds to the promoters of TGF-β target genes and recruits the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex to remove H3K27ac, resulting in silencing of profibrotic transcriptional programs. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal role for PRDM16 in maintaining epigenomic homeostasis during pulmonary fibrosis and underscore its potential as a promising therapeutic target for IPF.

papers.abstract_en: Previous studies have shown that signal regulatory protein γ (SIRPγ) is an important regulatory factor for T cell function. However, its expression and biological role in tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remain unknown. In this study, we find that the level of SIRPγ is significantly upregulated in TPE compared to non-TPE. Furthermore, we demonstrate SIRPγ involvement in TPE pathogenesis through the induction of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, SIRPγ interacts with CD47 to activate the phosphatidylinositol 3/kinase-protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway, leading to the upregulation of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) and the enhancement of serine metabolism. Serine, in turn, facilitates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) epigenetic modification at the NFATC2 locus. This modification, in coordination with TCR-induced calcium signaling, promotes NFATC2 activation, ultimately driving the expression of exhaustion-associated transcription factors and immunosuppressive receptors. Together, our findings identify SIRPγ as a regulator of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion in TPE and suggest its potential as a predictive biomarker for TPE diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: Weight loss is a prevalent symptom in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Nevertheless, the role of microplastics (MPs) in this process remains poorly understood, and the underlying mechanisms are still unknown. We measured 13 MPs types by pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in sputum from 40 COPD patients. Body composition was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis. A hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis explored the potential molecular mechanisms linking MPs exposure to alterations of body composition in COPD. Of the 40 participants, 12 (30.0%) were classified as underweight. Disease stage, nutritional status, and inflammatory indicators did not differ significantly between the two groups. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) was detected in 97.5% of samples and showed the highest median concentration. PVC and total MPs showed non-linear positive associations with the odds of underweight in COPD, with fully adjusted odds ratios of 4.324 and 4.497. Sensitivity analyses also acquired the similar results. Higher PVC and total MPs were associated with reduced fat mass (P < 0.05), and linear regression models adjusted for all covariables showed similar negative associations. Exploratory mediation analysis showed that after adjustment for fat mass, the negative association between PVC exposure and body mass index (BMI) was no longer observed, suggesting that this association may be explained by reduced fat mass. Using the low-molecular-weight constituents of PVC and its additives (vinyl chloride monomer and phthalates) as the exposure sources, hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis identified 84 targets shared with COPD and weight loss, enriched in inflammatory and adipocyte-differentiation signaling (adjusted P = 8.4 × 10⁻15 and 2.1 × 10⁻10). In conclusion, sputum MPs exposure was associated with higher odds of underweight and with lower fat mass in COPD patients. Chemicals-driven inflammatory signaling and impaired adipocyte differentiation may be involved in MPs-associated weight loss in COPD, which needs to be verified by experimental evidences.
